_comment: THE COMPONENT CATALOGUE — the single source of truth for what a manifest may name.
Read by TWO consumers and there is deliberately only ONE file:
- worker-v2/src/arms/registry.ts binds these ids to code and asserts at boot that
every `implemented` id has an implementation and no `unimplemented` id does;
- evaluation/arms/verify.mjs validates manifests and reports maturity blockers.
A mirrored catalogue would drift, and a drifted catalogue is a flag by another name.
`status` says whether the component EXISTS AS CODE. It does NOT say whether the
registry binds it to a callable — that is governed by types.ts#WIRED_SLOTS, and today
only the `plan` slot is wired. The two were conflated in the first version of this file
and the cost was concrete: resolving the BASELINE manifest demanded a callable for
`ingest: v2-two-pass`, which exists as code but is reached by DIRECT IMPORT and has no
registry entry — correctly — so the no-manifest path threw and four green workflow tests
went red. resolve.ts now calls validateComponent() for all five slots and componentFor()
only for wired ones.
implemented   — the code exists and runs today. Reached through the registry if its
slot is WIRED, by direct import otherwise. Both are real.
unimplemented — the slot is declared and typed; invoking it THROWS. A manifest may
name it (so the manifest is checkable and the deploy resolves), and
verify.mjs reports it as a MATURITY blocker rather than a config error.
An id ABSENT from this file is UNRESOLVED_COMPONENT and is fatal at resolve time, for
every slot, wired or not. That is the check a real arm's typo must not survive.
See evaluation/arms/ARCHITECTURE.md §2 for the slot semantics and §9 for why the
unimplemented ones are unimplemented.

ingest.pinnedReason: PRE-REGISTRATION.md §8.1 shared-ingestion control. Arms consuming different parsers would measure PARSERS and report the answer as ARCHITECTURE.

v2-two-pass.note: the baseline. Grok whole-document + DeepSeek block-by-block, merged and sealed.

shared-sealed.note: THE CONTROL. Consumes a contract revision sealed ONCE, outside every arm, by id. Every arm manifest must name the SAME revision; verify.mjs fails INGEST_DIVERGENCE otherwise.

none.note: the baseline and arm A: obligations are a flat scoped list, there is no routing graph.

routing-graph.binds: src/structure/index.ts#compileStructureModel — compiles a routing graph from the sealed contract revision's typed case data

plan.note: THE C vs C-R SEAM, and the only slot where they differ.

v2-two-tier.note: the baseline. Deterministic: zero model calls, zero I/O, zero site knowledge.

model-attested.blocker: arm A as PRE-REGISTRATION.md §1.1 defines it — a model that navigates and decides what to test — has never been built. worker-v2 plans deterministically. ARCHITECTURE.md §11.1 is the resulting amendment.

random-equal-size.blocker: depends on structure=routing-graph. Construction is fully pinned by PRE-REGISTRATION.md §5.6: uniform draw over VALID executable traversals, matched to C on DISTINCT NODE-VISITS within +/-10%, seed pinned per (surveyId, repeat).

traverse.pinnedReason: Browser mechanics are not an architecture. A per-arm driver would put an uncontrolled 'whose click handling is better' term into every comparison. It also keeps the visit log HARNESS-owned, without which coverage_honesty (§4.5) is unmeasurable.

harness-walk.note: the scored-run walker. Lives in the HARNESS, not in the arm. ARCHITECTURE.md §7.

v2-deterministic.note: the baseline. Deterministic over observations + the sealed contract; no model call is permitted in it (run-workflow.ts structural commitment #3).

deterministic-diff.blocker: arm B's edge-set arithmetic. graph-spike/diff.mjs levelA/levelB/levelC exist but take (manifest, graphS) — same input problem as structure=routing-graph.

model-freeform.blocker: arm A's model judgement. See model-attested.

model-attribute.blocker: BLOCKED BY INVARIANT, not by missing code. verify-observations.ts promotes to `verified` ONLY via a closed predicate over a TYPED expectation sealed in the contract; derive-verdicts.ts forbids model calls outright. Both are the fix for nine fabricated verdicts and must not be relaxed. The legitimate path is a typed ModelAttributeObservation that derivation reads deterministically — which needs an OWNER RULING on whether a model-attested observation may earn `verified`. ARCHITECTURE.md §9.3.
